reasons: The redline reaches the playbook's preferred position: the grant now runs to Customer, its affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf, the at-will 'revocable' (and 'non-transferable, non-assignable') language is removed, and transfer to an M&A successor is expressly permitted.

Revocation is not deleted outright but tied to termination under paragraph 4, which preserves the existing bargain (30-day cure / post-Initial-Term notice) and remains consistent with paragraph 21(c)(ii) revoking the licence on termination; the no-sublicense restriction is retained, so the edit is proportionate rather than over-reaching.

The high changed-character ratio (0.637) is explained by the need to restructure the adjective string in the grant sentence ('non-transferable, non-assignable ... revocable license'); the operative second sentence and all other terms are untouched, so this is an acceptable whole-clause rewrite, not scope creep.
Replacing 'non-transferable, non-assignable' with successor-only transferability does not create a broader assignment loophole, since general assignment remains governed by paragraph 9(h) as cited.
The comment is accurate, first-person plural, concise, correctly cites the playbook rationale and offers the affiliates-on-written-notice fallback.
